answer: A strong sybil defense is random mutual-audit quorums. High-value transactions must be co-signed by a small quorum of peers drawn at random from the whole network, never chosen by the agent itself. A real agent builds a diverse trail of co-signatures, a pulse other agents can verify. A sybil farm cannot staff its own quorums, because random selection mirrors the network's true mix rather than the attacker cluster. Fresh accounts with no audit history are like a lotus with no roots: they look fine but fail quorum checks, so they stay locked out of large trades until they earn peer audits.
